edges.reason: The equal-addend sum being rewritten as a product contains chained addition. The subtraction half of the endpoint is not required.
Seven/eight/nine products can be built independently by equal groups; the earlier two-through-six fact table is useful preparation but not a logical requirement to learn those products.
The target explicitly includes the multiplication-division relation, so multiplication meaning is needed for that inverse-operation assertion.

The general digit-by-digit multiplication algorithm contains digit products with seven, eight and nine. Their values are required, without demanding rote recitation as the exclusive way to obtain them.

The earlier one-digit long-division workflow is analogous but is not a mathematical suboperation needed to divide by a two-digit divisor. Division meaning, place value, trial products and subtraction suffice to learn the new workflow directly.
edges.scope: Familiarity with a similar long-division layout before learning two-digit divisors

edges.reason: Two-digit-divisor trial products multiply the divisor by one quotient digit, not two two-digit numbers. The two-by-two written product is broader useful practice rather than a prerequisite.

Two-digit division broadens which expression steps can be computed. The precedence convention and a three-step calculation can also be practiced with one-digit divisors; the wider algorithm is preparation.
